name: Diclofenac
summary: A potent analgesic and anti-inflammatory NSAID with strong pain relief but a less forgiving safety profile than many alternatives.
good: Short courses of inflammatory pain when strong symptomatic relief is needed.
bad: High cardiovascular-risk patients, chronic unsupervised use, or anyone already stacked with bleeding-risk drugs.
clinicalPearls: It can feel impressively effective, which is exactly why it gets overused.
mechanism: Nonselective COX inhibition reduces prostaglandin synthesis and inflammatory pain.
indications: Acute musculoskeletal pain, arthritis flares, and short-term inflammatory pain where potency matters.
interactionNotes: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, corticosteroids, SSRIs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics increase risk.

warnings: CV risk, GI toxicity, renal effects, and liver enzyme elevation deserve respect.

Functionally closer to the COX-2-selective agents than its "nonselective" label suggests — a good illustration that selectivity is a spectrum, not a category.
Present, though somewhat lower than some other nonselective agents at matched anti-inflammatory doses, consistent with its COX-2 lean.
Elevated — comparable in magnitude to some COX-2-selective inhibitors in large observational studies, prompting the same cardiovascular caution.
Available topically (gel) for localized joint/soft-tissue pain with substantially lower systemic exposure and risk.
